learning_objective: 🎯 Master the balance of chemical reactions! Understand how reversible reactions stabilize, learn Le Chatelier's principle to control them, and calculate the pH of acids and bases.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Equilibrium doesn't mean the reaction has stopped. It means the Forward reaction rate exactly equals the Backward reaction rate. It looks completely still from the outside, like walking down an up-escalator at the exact same speed!

A mathematical ratio of product concentrations to reactant concentrations at equilibrium. If $K_c$ is very large, the reaction heavily favors products. If $K_c$ is very small, it heavily favors reactants.

If you stress a system at equilibrium (by changing temperature, pressure, or concentration), the system will shift to relieve that stress. For example, adding more reactants pushes the reaction forward to make more products.

Arrhenius said acids give $H^+$ and bases give $OH^-$. Bronsted-Lowry said acids donate protons, bases accept them. The pH scale measures $H^+$ concentration logarithmically ($pH = -\log[H^+]$). Neutral is 7, acids are lower, bases are higher.
Buffer solutions resist changes in their pH even when small amounts of strong acid or strong base are added. Our human blood is an incredibly precise natural buffer system!

fun_activity.title: ☕ The Tea Bag Balance
fun_activity.instructions: Dip a tea bag into hot water. At first, the color leaves the bag rapidly (forward reaction). After a few minutes, the color of the water stops getting darker. The tea particles are still moving in and out of the bag, but at the EXACT same rate (Dynamic Equilibrium)!

exam_tips: 📌 Pure solids and pure liquids have a constant concentration and are taken as $1$ (unity) when writing the $K_c$ expression.
📌 The relationship between $K_p$ and $K_c$ is a guaranteed question: $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n}$, where $\Delta n$ is the change in moles of gaseous products minus gaseous reactants.
📌 Remember that adding a Catalyst speeds up both the forward and backward reactions equally. It helps reach equilibrium faster, but it NEVER changes the equilibrium constant ($K_c$).
quick_recap: ⭐ An increase in pressure shifts the equilibrium towards the side with fewer moles of gas.
⭐ The conjugate base of a strong acid is always a weak base, and vice versa.
⭐ Precipitation occurs only when the Ionic Product exceeds the Solubility Product ($K_{sp}$).
